conviction_note: No pre-release and no analyst consensus. The bar is the company's own guide: operational adjusted EBITDA of USD 60-70m for FY26, which implies USD 13-18m a quarter in H2, plus SOMA's raised USD 360-390m guide. Four small positives point mildly up: no profit warning this year, where both issuers cut on 9 Oct 2025 ahead of Q3; North Sea AHTS spot rates held through Aug-Sep at 3-6x last year; dividend capacity is rising; order intake since Q2. A known one-off in Q2 points the other way. So the findings sum to +1.3 while the scaled number is +0.7 (p_up 57 x abs 5.0). The gap is intended: each finding is an inference or a proxy that lands inside the guide, and the 2025 Q3 print fell 4.2% even though its miss was pre-warned.

findings.finding: Neither SOFF nor its 27.3% associate SOMA has issued a guidance update or trading update before this Q3. On 9 Oct 2025 both filed inside-information guidance cuts before the Q3 print, citing a weak North Sea AHTS spot market and CSV idle time. Silence through 3 Nov under MAR art. 17 indicates the FY26 guides (operational 60-70m; SOMA 360-390m) are not materially missed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: guidance cut pre-released 9 Oct 2025 (SOFF adj. EBITDA 120-150m cut to ~115m), and the print still fell 4.16% on 30 Oct 2025. Q2 2026, when SOMA raised its guide: SOFF +1.92%.
findings.why_not_priced: Absence is not reported anywhere. If the market had read it as a clean quarter, the stock would not have drifted -4.4% over 5 days into the print (69.0 sealed vs 72.3 on Oct 9-19). No analyst preview exists to carry it.
findings.independence: Seabrokers Sep 2026 monthly report: large North Sea AHTS spot averaged £110,702/day vs £37,599 a year earlier (https://seabrokers.no/chartering/seabreeze/market-report-september-2026/)

findings.finding: North Sea AHTS spot rates for large vessels (>22,000 bhp) held high through Q3 2026: about £102k in July, £96k in August and £111k in September, against roughly £15-38k in Q3 2025. Utilisation ran 55/73/61%. This is SOMA's spot AHTS exposure (three vessels), which was the named cause of the Q3 2025 cut. Rates stayed firm after SOMA's guide was set on 15 July, so SOMA's associate contribution leans to the upper half of its guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: a weak AHTS spot market caused the SOMA/SOFF guidance cut and SOFF fell 4.16% on the print. Q2 2026: record AHTS rates and a SOMA guide raise, SOFF +1.92%.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-01 (September 2026 report); August and July reports at /market-report-august-2026/ and /market-report-july-2026/
findings.why_not_priced: This is a broker PDF series that nobody covering SOFF aggregates, and the effect reaches SOFF only through a 27.3% equity-accounted stake. It is a proxy for an associate's segment, so it stays small. Also, Q3 rates sit about 20% below Q2's record (Q2 averaged ~USD 175k per Spinergie), so QoQ the AHTS line is down.

findings.finding: Dividend capacity is rising into the Q3 declaration. The SOFF dividend went USD 0.05 (Q3'25), 0.05, 0.10, 0.15 (Q2'26, USD 12.4m), roughly tracking SOFF's share of the SOMA dividend (~USD 13m in Q2). At its Q2 mid-guide SOMA paid ~USD 47m a quarter against ~USD 293m of FCFE, under a policy of paying out the majority. SOFF also expects ~USD 14.5m of arbitration cash not yet in its Q2 accounts. And on 6 Oct the 'preserving cash' constraint for the Maximus option became a debt-financed purchase.
findings.why_not_priced: At USD 0.15 a quarter and NOK 69 (USDNOK 9.25) the yield is already about 8%, and the stock has not re-rated toward a higher payout: it is flat since the 15 Jul print (68.9 to 69.0). If the market expected another step to 0.20, the run-up would not be negative. A hold at 0.15 against a pattern of +0.05 steps is the downside, hence the wide range.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 5.0. The numbers are new (no pre-release this year), and both issuers carry FY guides that can change in the release. The name's own 2.9% median reaction stays context, not a cap. It stays below the 7% European base because realised vol is low (26% annualised, 1.6% a day).

'A finding about a number already told is worth 0' / 'one-off beat is sold': checked. The Q2 arbitration one-off is kept at -0.2 and nothing rests on a pre-released number. Finding sizes are unchanged.
